skill.name: clinicaltrials-database
skill.description: Query ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 for trial searches, NCT ID lookups, study details, pagination, summaries, and CSV exports.
skill.summary: Search ClinicalTrials.gov and summarize trial records with API v2 helpers.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, public ClinicalTrials.gov requests, and bounded CSV export samples. Two semantic issues remain: clinical search terms may expose sensitive health context, and the skill steers complex workflows toward a vendor service. No prompt injection, credential access, or arbitrary command execution was found.

remediation.issue: Clinical search terms may include sensitive health context.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy notice that users should not include patient identifiers or protected health information in search terms.

remediation.issue: The skill contains promotional steering toward K-Dense Web.
remediation.suggestion: Remove marketplace-unrelated promotional steering from SKILL.md or move it outside agent instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Health Search Terms May Be Sent to External API
semantic_findings.description: The skill supports patient matching and sends condition, intervention, location, and sponsor filters to ClinicalTrials.gov. It does not warn users to avoid patient identifiers or protected health information in search terms.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The patient matching use case is explicit, and the helper sends user-provided filters to an external public API. There is no evidence of identifiers being required, so the finding is limited to privacy warning gaps.

semantic_findings.title: Promotional Steering to External Service
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the assistant to proactively suggest K-Dense Web for complex workflows. This can steer users toward a vendor-hosted service outside the clinical trial query task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and appears in the skill text. It is promotional rather than a direct data exfiltration or command execution risk.

content.value_statement: Clinical trial searches can be slow when users need filters, status checks, and study details. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 queries, summaries, and CSV exports.
actual_capabilities: Searches ClinicalTrials.gov by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, phase, and NCT ID.
Retrieves detailed study records through ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 endpoints.
Explains API parameters, status values, pagination, response modules, and rate limits.
Summarizes key trial fields such as title, status, phase, enrollment, dates, and eligibility.
Shows how to export trial search results to CSV for analysis.
limitations: Requires network access to ClinicalTrials.gov for live API queries.
Depends on ClinicalTrials.gov data quality, availability, and rate limits.
Does not provide medical advice or confirm patient eligibility for a trial.
May not include unpublished trials or studies missing from ClinicalTrials.gov.

use_cases.title: Match Patients to Recruiting Studies
use_cases.description: Search for recruiting trials by condition, location, intervention, and status before reviewing eligibility criteria.

use_cases.title: Analyze Research Activity
use_cases.description: Collect trial records for a disease area and compare sponsors, phases, enrollment, and update dates.

use_cases.title: Track Drug Development
use_cases.description: Find studies for a drug or device and review current trial status, phase, locations, and sponsors.

prompt_templates.title: Search by Condition
prompt_templates.prompt: Find recruiting ClinicalTrials.gov studies for type 2 diabetes in California. Summarize the top results with NCT IDs and locations.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Trial
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve details for NCT04852770. Summarize the title, status, phase, sponsor, enrollment, eligibility, and site contacts.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Interventions
prompt_templates.scenario: Filtered search across a treatment area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for Phase 3 pembrolizumab trials that are recruiting or active. Compare conditions, sponsors, enrollment, and result availability.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Export Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 workflow to collect all recruiting rare disease trials, handle pagination, respect rate limits, and export a CSV summary.

output_examples.input: Find recruiting lung cancer trials in New York.
output: A ranked list of matching studies with NCT IDs, titles, recruitment status, phases, and New York locations.
A short note explaining which filters were used and how many records matched.

output_examples.input: Summarize one NCT record for eligibility review.
output: A concise trial profile with title, sponsor, phase, enrollment, summary, age range, sex criteria, and major exclusions.
A reminder to verify eligibility with the trial team before making clinical decisions.

output_examples.input: Prepare a CSV export for Alzheimer studies.
output: A planned set of fields for export, including NCT ID, title, status, phase, sponsor, enrollment, and last update.
Guidance on page size, pagination, and rate limits for the export run.

best_practices: Use broad condition terms first, then narrow by status, phase, intervention, and location.
Avoid patient identifiers or protected health information in API search terms.
Respect rate limits and use pagination for large result sets.
anti_patterns: Treating API results as medical advice or final eligibility decisions.
Running bulk exports without page limits, backoff, or a clear field plan.
Assuming every trial record has complete contacts, results, dates, or eligibility details.

faq.question: Does this skill need an API key?
faq.answer: No. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 is public and does not require authentication.

faq.question: Can it find trials by NCT ID?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for retrieving detailed study records by NCT identifier.

faq.question: Can it export results?
faq.answer: Yes. The references show how to request CSV output and save selected study fields.

faq.question: Does it decide whether a patient qualifies?
faq.answer: No. It can review eligibility text, but trial teams must confirm eligibility.

faq.question: What data source does it use?
faq.answer: It uses ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, maintained by the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

faq.question: Can it handle large searches?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains pagination, page size limits, and rate limit handling for larger searches.
